findings.title: `report.json` shape is not validated at the load boundary
findings.description: `BatchReport.load()` casts `report["items"]` to `list[dict[str, object]]` instead of validating it, then `BatchItemRecord.from_json()` calls `.get()` on each item at `src/squadron/pipeline/batch_report.py:164`. A malformed but syntactically valid JSON report such as `{"schemaVersion": 1, ..., "items": ["bad"]}` or `"items": [null]` raises an uncaught `AttributeError`; the `except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError)` at `src/squadron/pipeline/batch_report.py:331-335` does not catch it. `item_resume._validate()` only converts `BatchReportLoadError` into a REJECTED exit, so this path escapes as a traceback instead of the documented exit 2. The written `docType` at `src/squadron/pipeline/batch_report.py:286` is also never checked on load. The current tests cover missing, unparseable, and wrong-version reports, but not malformed item shapes.

findings.title: Item-resume flags are not mutually exclusive with other run modes
findings.description: `check_item_flags()` at `src/squadron/cli/commands/run_item.py:32-48` only validates relationships among `--item`, `--resume`, `--decision`, and `--instructions`. It does not reject item-resume flags combined with `--validate`, `--step-done`, `--prompt-only --next`, or similar command modes. Because the pipeline-required guard in `run()` excludes cases where `resume is not None`, a command such as `sq run --validate --resume r1 --item 401 --decision retry` reaches `assert pipeline is not None` at `src/squadron/cli/commands/run.py:1150` and crashes. Other earlier dispatch arms, such as `--step-done` and `--prompt-only --next --resume`, exit before the `--resume --item` block, so the item-resume flags are silently ignored. `tests/cli/commands/test_run_item.py` covers only item-flag combinations and a plain resume, not these conflicting modes.

findings.title: Run-lock mutation detection misses executor shapes that commit
findings.description: `_step_mutates()` only recognizes a top-level `StepTypeName.LOOP` with `commit_each_iteration: true` and recursively walks `config["steps"]`. However `_execute_step()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/executor.py:721-748` also supports a legacy inline `loop:` sub-config on other step types, and `_execute_fan_out_step()` expands `fan_out.inner` through `_execute_step_once()`. A custom pipeline with a non-mutating step type plus `loop: {commit_each_iteration: true, ...}`, or a `fan_out.inner` that expands to `devlog`/`commit`, can mutate git/cf while `pipeline_mutates()` returns `False`; `_take_run_lock()` will skip the lock. That contradicts the documented D11 rule that any pipeline which commits or moves cf state takes the lock. `tests/cli/commands/test_run_lock_cli.py` covers a top-level `loop` step and nested `steps`, but not inline `loop:` or `fan_out.inner`.

findings.title: A timed-out merge-base read is reported as "branch not merged"
findings.description: `_select_item()` calls `run_git(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ...])`; `run_git` returns `None` on timeout or invocation failure. At `src/squadron/pipeline/item_resume.py:297-303`, the code conflates that unknown result with a definite non-ancestor: it rewrites the status to `"complete but {branch} is not merged into {target}"`, then raises `_Stop(REJECTED, ...)`. The caller sees a normal validation refusal rather than an explicit "could not verify git state" failure, even though the new I/O path can hang, time out, or fail to answer. `tests/pipeline/test_item_resume_source.py` tests the real "not merged" case but has no test asserting the timeout/unknown-answer signal, which the failure-mode rules require for this new I/O path.

findings.title: Markdown and JSON reports are not atomic as a pair
findings.description: `BatchReport.write()` replaces the Markdown file first and the JSON file second. Each file is individually atomic, but the pair is not: if the second `_write_atomic()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/batch_report.py:308` fails, Markdown already contains the new record while JSON still contains the old one. `resume_item()` catches that `OSError` and returns `HALTED`, but the two report formats now disagree, contrary to the contract that a failed report rewrite leaves the old record in place. `tests/pipeline/test_batch_report.py::test_a_failed_write_keeps_the_previous_report_and_logs_error` patches `Path.replace` globally, so the first replace fails before the second call; it does not exercise the partial-success path.

structured_findings.summary: `report.json` shape is not validated at the load boundary
Item-resume flags are not mutually exclusive with other run modes
Run-lock mutation detection misses executor shapes that commit
A timed-out merge-base read is reported as "branch not merged"
Markdown and JSON reports are not atomic as a pair
